name: Mathematical Reasoning
definition: The ability to choose the right mathematical methods or formulas to solve a problem.

benchmark.name: Math23K
benchmark.metric: answer accuracy (%) on the Math23K public test set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: working adults who routinely apply elementary arithmetic reasoning at work (quantities, rates, proportions, simple equations).

benchmark.name: MATH
benchmark.model_or_system: GPT-2 1.5B pretrained on AMPS and fine-tuned on MATH (model identity from recall; the 6.9% figure is verified)
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the MATH test set, final answer checked for exact equivalence
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: adults who use mathematical reasoning at work, such as technicians, analysts and engineers-in-training, rather than competition mathematicians.

benchmark.name: MATH
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%), final-answer match on the MATH test set
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce that applies mathematical reasoning at work (engineers, analysts, accountants, technicians, STEM-degree holders). These are not competition-math specialists.

benchmark.name: MATH
benchmark.model_or_system: GPT-4 Code Interpreter with explicit code-based self-verification (CSV) and verification-guided weighted majority voting
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the MATH test set, final-answer exact match
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce that applies mathematical reasoning at work (engineers, analysts, scientists, quantitative professionals), not competition specialists

benchmark.name: MATH
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce that routinely applies mathematical reasoning at work (engineers, analysts, quantitative and STEM professionals)

benchmark.name: FrontierMath
benchmark.metric: percent of problems solved (accuracy), FrontierMath Tier 1-3
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce that applies mathematical reasoning at work (engineers, quantitative analysts, scientists, math-heavy professionals). Professional research mathematicians are the upper tail.

benchmark.name: FrontierMath
benchmark.metric: accuracy (% of problems solved, all-or-nothing), FrontierMath v2 Tiers 1-3 private set
benchmark.human_reference: Specialist workforce: professional mathematicians and highly quantitative workers (math PhDs, quantitative researchers) who routinely choose and apply advanced mathematical methods at work.
